title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations

body:
Google has announced a significant update to its AI generation tools, allowing users to remove visible watermarks from their generated content. This change aims to provide users with more flexibility and control over the final appearance of their AI-generated images and text.

What happened

In a recent update, Google introduced a feature that permits users to disable the visible watermark that typically accompanies AI-generated outputs. This decision comes as part of Google’s ongoing efforts to enhance user experience and streamline the integration of AI tools into creative workflows. While users can now opt to remove the visible watermark, it is important to note that this change does not affect the invisible benchmarks that remain embedded in the files. These invisible markers are designed to help identify AI-generated content, ensuring that the integrity of the identification process is maintained even when the visible watermark is absent.

Why it matters

The ability to remove visible watermarks from AI-generated content is a notable development in the realm of digital creativity. For artists, designers, and content creators, the presence of a watermark can sometimes detract from the aesthetic quality of their work. By allowing users to remove these visible markers, Google is acknowledging the need for a more polished and professional output, which can be particularly beneficial for those who wish to use AI tools for commercial purposes or public displays. Furthermore, the retention of invisible benchmarks ensures that while users have more freedom in presentation, there is still a mechanism in place to track and identify AI-generated content. This balance between user autonomy and content identification is crucial as the use of AI in creative fields continues to grow.

Source: techcrunch.com.
